title: Will the Community beat Dylan Matthews in the Metaculus Cup Summer 2026?
rc: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, at the conclusion of the Metaculus Cup Summer 2026, the Community Prediction has a greater Total Score than Dylan Matthews in the tournament leaderboard.
fp: This question will resolve after all other Metaculus Cup Summer 2026 questions have resolved and will not be included in the scoring used to determine whether the Community Prediction outperformed Dylan Matthews.

title: Will any match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup be delayed by more than 30 minutes due to extreme heat?
rc: This question will resolve as **Yes** if at least one match in the 2026 FIFA World Cup is delayed (kickoff postponed or play suspended) by 30 consecutive minutes or more and an official source (i.e., FIFA or an official referee) explicitly states that the reason for the delay is heat or high temperature.
bg:
Extreme heat [is expected in 14 out of 16 host cities](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40279-026-02398-4) of the 2026 FIFA World Cup 2026. The Professional Football Players Trade Union (FIFPRO) [recommends](https://media.fifpro.org/media/ltio1czh/heat-guidelines_en-1.pdf) that matches should be delayed or postponed when temperatures are above 28 degrees celsius ([WBGT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet-bulb_globe_temperature)). 

For the 2026 World Cup, [FIFA has instituted mandatory cooling breaks](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/dec/08/fifa-world-cup-2026-cooling-br

title: Will any U.S. state or EU member state restrict large-scale data center grid connections before September 2026?
rc:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, at any point before September 1, 2026, either a U.S. state or an EU member state announces a new moratorium, suspension, or binding restrictive rule applying to new grid connection requests from large-scale data centers, and the restriction is not officially reversed or rescinded before September 1, 2026, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

Large-scale datacenters are defined as facilities with contracted or requested grid capacity of 50 MW or more.
fp:
A **Yes** resolution requires a binding administrative order, enacted regulation, official policy directive, or other formal written statement with the force of law. Draft proposals open for public comment, preliminary consultations, and non-binding guidance documents do not qualify. Actions by transmission system operators acting without a formal government or regulatory mandate also will not cause this question to resolve as **Yes**.

A **Yes** resolution also requires a new restriction that did not exist before May 20, 2026, in substantially the same form. Renewals, extensions, or reaffirmations of pre-existing restrictions do not qualify.

Actions taken by organs of the U.S. federal government (e.g., FERC, DOE) will not cause this question to resolve as **Yes**.
bg:
The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure has placed unprecedented pressure on electricity grids across the United States and Europe. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) [projected in January 2026](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/Jan26.pdf) that electricity demand growth will accelerate significantly, with large computing facilities identified as a primary driver. The U.S. Department of Energy has [similarly identified data centers](https://www.energy.gov/oe/clean-energy-resources-meet-data-center-electricity-demand) as a critical short-term demand factor.

title: Will Shakira's "Dai Dai" outpeak Shakira's "Waka Waka" on the Billboard Hot 100?
rc:
This question resolves **Yes** if "Dai Dai" by Shakira & Burna Boy achieves a peak position on the Billboard Hot 100 (US) of #37 or higher at any point on or before July 31, 2026.

The peak position will be determined according to the weekly [Billboard Hot 100 charts](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/).
fp:
Remixes, regional versions, and language variants of "Dai Dai" (or any other official song) will be treated as the same song for purposes of this question; the highest-charting version counts.

The Billboard Hot 100 (US version) is the chart of record. Other Billboard charts (e.g., Global 200, Hot Latin Songs) do not count for resolution.
bg:

title: Will Pope Leo XIV visit another country other than Spain before September 2026?
rc:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if Pope Leo XIV officially visits a country other than Spain or Italy after May 18, 2026 and before September 1, 2026, according to the official [Vatican calendar of events for the Pope](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/events/year.dir.html/2026.html). Merely passing through a country's airspace, landing at an airport or otherwise making a transitory visit will not count towards resolution.

If Pope Leo XIV ceases to be Pope before September 2026 this question will be **annulled**.
fp: For the purpose of this question a country is defined as [a member state](https://www.un.org/en/about-us/member-states) according to the United Nations.
bg:
Papal travel outside Rome has historically been rare. Since [Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI") (1963–1978), however, more pastoral trips have occurred. With advances in technology, mass media and global connectivity, as well as a shift in the Church's leadership, the [Pope's international travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_travel) has become more common.

title: Will a new High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina officially be in place before September 2, 2026?
rc: This question will resolve as **Yes** if a successor to Christian Schmidt is announced and begins their tenure in the role of the High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina before September 2, 2026, according to [the OHR](https://www.ohr.int/?lang=en).
fp: If, before September 2, 2026, the High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina is replaced by another position, this question will be **annulled**. But if the OHR is closed without being replaced, the question will resolve as **No**.
bg: The High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina, together with the Office of the High Representative (OHR) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, was created in 1995 immediately after the signing of the [Dayton Agreement](https://www.ohr.int/dayton-peace-agreement/ "Dayton Agreement") ([Annex 10](https://www.ohr.int/dayton-peace-agreement/annex-10/)), which ended the 1992-1995 [Bosnian War](https://www.britannica.com/event/Bosnian-War "Bosnian War"). title: Will OpenAI's ChatGPT Atlas browser be released for Windows before September 1, 2026?
rc: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before September 1, 2026 UTC, OpenAI publicly releases ChatGPT Atlas for Windows.
fp:
An invite-only or otherwise individually selected rollout will not count as a public release. Only releases available to the general public will qualify.

A product by a different name will nevertheless count as "ChatGPT Atlas" if it is (1) a web browser that features ChatGPT, (2) released by OpenAI, and (3) treated by OpenAI as equivalent or a successor to ChatGPT Atlas.
bg:

title: Will at least 5 non-passengers be linked to the MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak before August 2026?
rc: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before August 1, 2026, at least five hantavirus cases are publicly reported in people who were not aboard the *MV Hondius* during its March-April 2026 voyage, and the cases are linked to the *MV Hondius* outbreak by a public health authority.
fp: A qualifying case must be either laboratory-confirmed or described as a probable/suspected hantavirus case linked to the *MV Hondius* outbreak. The case does not need to be conclusively proven to result from human-to-human transmission.
bg: In early May 2026, WHO [reported](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON599) a cluster of hantavirus infections associated with the cruise ship [MV *Hondius*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Hondius_hantavirus_outbreak), with seven confirmed or suspected cases and three deaths. The vessel carried [147 passengers and crew](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON599), and illness onset among reported cases ranged from April 6 to April 28, 2026. title: Will the UK National Threat Level reduce from SEVERE before September 2026?
rc:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before September 1, 2026, UTC, the JTAC reduces the UK National Threat Level (to LOW, MODERATE or SUBSTANTIAL) and that reduction takes effect. 

If a lower threat level is announced but does not come into effect until on or after September 1, 2026, that will not suffice to resolve this question as Yes.
fp:
The Northern Ireland-related Terrorism in Northern Ireland threat level is irrelevant to this question.

If the threat levels are renamed, this question will resolve as normal, provided that there is an unambiguous one-to-one correspondence between the old and the new threat levels. If the threat level system is discontinued or restructured such that there is no such one-to-one correspondence, the question will be annulled.
bg:
The Joint Terrorism Analysis Centre ([JTAC](https://www.mi5.gov.uk/about-us/joint-terrorism-analysis-centre)) is the United Kingdom’s independent authority for all-source terrorism assessment. JTAC is based within Military Intelligence, Section 5 ([MI5](https://www.mi5.gov.uk/about-us)), the UK's domestic counter-intelligence and security agency. 

On April 30, 2026, [the JTAC raised the UK National Threat Level](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-national-threat-level-raised-to-severe) (England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland) from SUBSTANTIAL, meaning an attack is likely, to SE

title: Will Instructure be subject to another major hack before September 1, 2026?
rc:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, after the question's opening and before September 1, 2026, Instructure or any of its [products](https://www.instructure.com/products) (including but not limited to Canvas, Mastery, Parchment, and Impact) experiences at least one cybersecurity incident that meets any of the following conditions:

1. **Data exfiltration:** An unauthorized party obtains personal data (such as names, email addresses, student IDs, messages, credentials, or financial information) of at least 10,000 users.
2. **Service disruption:** One or more Instructure products are rendered substantially unavailable to at least 100 institutional customers for a continuous period of at least 4 hours as a direct result of a security breach.
3. **Ransom or extortion demand:** A threat actor issues a ransom or extortion demand related to data or systems access newly obtained from Instructure.

All conditions require confirmation from at least one of the following: Instructure official communications, credible news reporting, or government disclosures. An attacker's public claim alone will not be sufficient.
fp:
Incidents originating from upstream third-party vendors (e.g., Salesforce, AWS) do not count unless Instructure or its products were the primary target of the attack, even if such incidents result in the compromise of Instructure-held user data or disruption of Instructure-operated services.

Routine vulnerability disclosures, bug bounty reports, or patched vulnerabilities that do not result in actual unauthorized access or data loss do not count.

Continued fallout from the original April 29 to May 11, 2026 ShinyHunters breach, such as continued extortion demands based on, or disclosures of, already-stolen data, do not qualify.
bg:
Instructure is the company behind Canvas LMS, used by [41%](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Canvas_security_incident) of North American higher education institutions for coursework, exams, grading, and student communication. In the last eight months, it has been hacked twice by [ShinyHunters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ShinyHunters), a black-hat criminal hacking and extortion group.

title: Will another country announce they will quit OPEC or OPEC+ before September 2026?
rc:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if after May 1, 2026, and before September 1, 2026, any member country of OPEC or OPEC+ announces publicly that they will quit or suspend their membership to the alliance.

The date of the member country formally leaving the alliance does not have to occur within the time period for the question to resolve as **Yes**.
fp:
If the member country publicly announces they will quit the alliance but subsequently retracts their statement this question will still resolve as **Yes**.

Suspensions of quota obligations, while the country continues to be a member will not count towards resolution.
bg:

title: Will the Senate of the Philippines remove Vice President Sara Duterte from office before September 2026?
rc: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before September 1, 2026, the Senate of the Philippines convicts Vice President Sara Duterte on one or more articles of impeachment with the constitutionally required two-thirds majority vote, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
fp: This question relates only to the articles of impeachment approved by the House on May 11, 2026.
bg:
On May 11, 2026, the House of Representatives in the Philippines [voted 257-25 to impeach](https://apnews.com/article/philippines-vice-president-duterte-impeachment-5d619c24ae6ef880d3c03bbcdccc1536) Vice President Sara Duterte over "alleged unexplained wealth and threats against the president, as the rift between the camps of the country’s top two officials escalated." There were nine abstentions.
